messages.subject: Curious about flat traceplot
parts:
Hello all,

Occasionally, a Stan run will return a traceplot that looks like the one attached—a seemingly well-mixing run that suddenly flatlines when the adaptation period ends. I am curious why this happens and whether it is diagnostic of problems with the model. Thanks for the enlightenment!

Devin

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Curious about flat traceplot
parts:
The last thing that happens in warmup is that the step size
is adapted (the manual has a more detailed description of
adaptation). This targets an acceptance rate, and if it
can't get the acceptance rate high enough, it will reduce
the step size.

What is the tree depth during sampling (after warmup)?
And the step size? Do other parameters behave similarly?
Do other chains behave this way or do you have a rough idea of
what the posterior variance is supposed to be?

One possibility is that if you have varying curvature in
the posterior (as in the funnel example in the manual), Stan
can get stuck in the neck (low variance) of the funnel. This can
happen at any time. Technically, this is correct behavior to ensure
detailed balance, but it doesn't help you.

- Bob
